_README: THE CHARACTER LOCK. One place that says what each character looks like, so two pictures of the same
person cannot disagree. Nothing else in this repo is allowed to describe a locked character in prose.
HOW IT IS USED
docs/prompts.md writes {CafeWalker} inside a '> ' prompt line. tools/gen_images.py replaces that token
with 'prompt' below before it sends anything to the model, so every picture gets the SAME words.
tools/char_lock_check.py fails if a prompt writes a locked character out by hand instead.
WHY IT EXISTS
Fri Nov 13: the title card, the 'to be continued' card and the itch.io cover each drew the main
character's apron differently - a crossed X-back, a plain shirt back, and a bib with no neck strap at
all. Three pictures, three aprons. A player reads that as AI slop, correctly.
THE RULE FOR CHANGING ONE
'sheet' is the drawing the rigged 3D model was made from. It is the truth. If you change a lock you are
saying the MODEL is wrong, so the model gets remade too - never change a lock just to match a picture
that came out differently.
A COSTUME IS A FORM, NOT A SECOND CHARACTER. Sat Nov 14: the title card needs the main character twice in one
frame - barista and film director - so he now has {CafeWalker:director} alongside {CafeWalker}. A costume form
REPEATS the face, hair and the garments that do not change, and swaps only what does. Never add a second
character entry for the same person: two entries drift apart, which is the whole failure this file exists to
stop. If two of him appear in one picture, say in the prompt that they are one person with an identical face.
REDESIGNED Fri Nov 14 by the Team Owner: *"You can give the main character a whole new outfit if it works,
just get the point across that he becomes a director of reality when all powers have been collected."* The
charcoal bomber jacket became a long open charcoal black coat with a line of cyan power-light down each open
edge and three cyan rings on the right forearm - one ring per power. This is ALLOWED and is not the thing the
rule above forbids: there is no rigged model of the director costume yet, so no model was contradicted. The
moment a director model IS made, this entry becomes its truth and the no-editing rule applies to it as well.
A PROP IS NOT A COSTUME. The clapperboard came out of {CafeWalker:director} on Fri Nov 14 and lives in
{CafeWalker:director_board} instead. The title animation fades a clapperboard in OVER both figures as its
own separate element, so a board already in his hand would have given the shot two of them. Use the plain
:director form when something else in the shot supplies the board, :director_board when he should hold it.
The blank-slate invariant below still applies wherever a slate appears, in either form or on its own.
TORSO-UP FORMS: {CafeWalker:bust} and {CafeWalker:director_bust} are the same two costumes with the parts
below mid-chest left out, for a picture cropped at the chest. They exist because the full forms mention the
apron reaching below the knee and the sneakers, and a prompt that says 'chest upward only' AND 'below his
knees' is the same self-contradiction that made UI-TITLE2 take 1 come back side by side instead of back to
back - given two clauses that cannot both hold, this model drops one, and never the one you would choose.
Both bust forms KEEP the single neck loop and the bare-shirt back, because that is the detail that drifts.
SHORT FORM: write {CafeWalker:short} when the character is small or far away in the frame. It is the
same lock, shortened to the details that still read at that size - the apron's single neck loop and bare
back are kept in BOTH forms, because that is the detail that drifted.
'sheet_prompts' are the prompt codes that DREW the canonical sheet. They are the lock's own source,
so char_lock_check.py lets them describe the character in their own words. Nothing else may.
Changing one of those prompts means redrawing the sheet AND remaking the rigged model.
CAMERA ANGLE IS PART OF THE LOCK. If the detail that drifts lives on a surface the camera cannot see, the
model will invent that surface. The apron's single neck loop is the clearest example: drawn from directly
behind, the model reaches for the cross-back apron it has seen a thousand times and the words do not stop
it (three takes, three cross-backs). Pose a locked character so the distinguishing detail is IN FRAME -
side or three-quarter for this apron - or use --lock-ref and hand the model the sheet itself.
SAY WHAT IS THERE, NOT WHAT IS ABSENT. Sat Nov 14: the title card kept drawing a manufacturer badge on the
car through 'no badge, no emblem' in the prompt AND 'car badge' in the negative, and stopped the moment the
grille was described positively ('a plain black horizontal mesh grille whose centre is smooth and empty').
The apron straps were failing the same way - 'leaving his back bare with no crossed straps' is an absence,
and the model dropped it four takes running. Both straps clauses are now written as a positive description
of what the back actually looks like. THIS IS A REWORDING, NOT A CHANGE TO THE GARMENT: the apron is the
same single-neck-loop bib apron the rigged models wear. The rule still stands - if a lock ever has to change
what a character IS, the sheet is redrawn and the model remade instead.
GARMENT-ONLY FORM: {CafeWalker:apron} is the apron on its own, for a picture where the garment appears
without the person in it - the lose screen is his apron lying on a studio floor. Without this the lose
screen described the apron by hand and nothing was guarding it.

CafeWalker.role: the player character, a coffee shop worker
CafeWalker.prompt: a slim young man of about twenty-five with short messy straight black hair falling over his forehead and covering the tops of his ears, a thin calm tired face, wearing a khaki brown long-sleeve collared button shirt with the sleeves pushed up to just below the elbow and the collar open, over it a plain dark green bib apron held up by one single strap that rises from the two top corners of the bib and meets in a loop high behind his neck, so that seen from behind the whole of his back is plain khaki shirt with nothing on it except that one strap at the neck and the two waist ties passing round his waist to the front, one square patch pocket on the chest of the bib, the long apron waist ties brought round and knotted in a simple bow at the front of his waist just under the bib, a pale grey bar towel tucked into the waist tie at his left hip, the apron reaching below his knees, loose charcoal grey trousers and grey canvas low-top sneakers with white toe caps
CafeWalker.prompt_short: a slim young man with short messy black hair, wearing a khaki brown long-sleeve shirt with the sleeves pushed up and a dark green bib apron held up by one single strap that meets in a loop high behind his neck, his back otherwise plain khaki shirt with only the waist ties passing round it to a knot at the front
CafeWalker.prompt_apron: a plain dark green bib apron with one single strap looped to go over the head, a square patch pocket on the bib, and long waist ties
invariants: ONE neck loop. The apron goes over the head on a single strap. The back is bare shirt.
NEVER crossed straps, NEVER an X on the back, NEVER a two-strap cross-back apron.
The bib has one square chest pocket.
The waist ties knot at the FRONT, in a bow, under the bib. Not at the back.
A pale grey bar towel hangs at his left hip.
Sleeves are pushed up to below the elbow, forearms bare. Shirt is khaki brown, never cream.
The apron is below the knee, not a short waist apron.

COSTUMES, NOT PEOPLE: {CafeWalker:director} is the SAME man as {CafeWalker}. Same hair, same face, same khaki brown shirt underneath, same trousers, same shoes. Only the apron is swapped - for the long charcoal black coat - and nothing else about him changes.
The director's cyan is LIGHT along the open edges of the coat and three rings on a forearm. It is never a pattern printed on the cloth, never glowing eyes, never a whole glowing body.

THREE cyan forearm rings, one for each power collected. Never two, never four, never a number written anywhere. WHICH forearm is staging, not design: the canonical full figure ({CafeWalker:director}, {CafeWalker:director_bust}) wears them on his RIGHT, and {CafeWalker:director_half} - the half-body split title, where only his left arm is inside the director half - wears them on his LEFT. The count is the invariant; the arm is whichever one the camera can see.
He is bare-headed in both costumes. The director wears no hat of any kind and carries no megaphone.
The clapperboard's slate is one flat unbroken white panel. Its only marking is the striped clapper bar along the top edge.
CafeWalker.never: cream shirt, white shirt, crossed apron straps, cross-back apron, X straps on the back, apron with no neck strap, short waist apron, bare chest, tie, waistcoat, glasses, beard, blond hair, hat, beret, flat cap, baseball cap, director's cap, megaphone, sunglasses, writing on the clapperboard, letters on the slate, numbers on the slate, chalk writing, handwriting, bomber jacket, suit jacket, suit and tie, bow tie, waistcoat, cape, cloak, armour, crown, wings, glowing eyes, glowing body, neon patterns printed on cloth, circuit patterns, text on the coat, letters on the coat, numbers on the coat
CafeWalker.prompt_director: the same slim young man of about twenty-five with the same short messy straight black hair falling over his forehead and covering the tops of his ears and the same thin calm tired face, dressed now as the director of reality: a long charcoal black single-breasted coat worn open, its tall collar standing up behind his neck and its two front panels falling open and wide to either side, worn over the same khaki brown long-sleeve collared shirt with the collar open and the sleeves pushed up to just below the elbow, one narrow clean unbroken line of pale cyan light running down the inner edge of each open coat panel and up around the standing collar, three thin pale cyan rings banded one above another around his right forearm, the same loose charcoal grey trousers and the same grey canvas low-top sneakers with white toe caps
CafeWalker.prompt_director_short: the same young man with the same short messy black hair and the same face, in a long open charcoal black coat with a tall standing collar over the same khaki brown long-sleeve shirt, a line of pale cyan light down each open coat edge and three thin cyan rings around his right forearm
CafeWalker.prompt_director_board: the same slim young man of about twenty-five with the same short messy straight black hair falling over his forehead and covering the tops of his ears and the same thin calm tired face, dressed now as the director of reality: a long charcoal black single-breasted coat worn open, its tall collar standing up behind his neck and its two front panels falling open and wide to either side, worn over the same khaki brown long-sleeve collared shirt with the collar open and the sleeves pushed up to just below the elbow, one narrow clean unbroken line of pale cyan light running down the inner edge of each open coat panel and up around the standing collar, three thin pale cyan rings banded one above another around his right forearm, the same loose charcoal grey trousers and the same grey canvas low-top sneakers with white toe caps, and a small black film clapperboard held up at shoulder height in one hand whose slate is one flat unbroken smooth white panel and whose top edge is a plain black and white striped clapper bar

CafeCoworker.prompt: a young woman of about twenty-four with dark brown hair pulled back into a short high ponytail and a loose fringe, wearing a pure white short-sleeve collared shirt and over it a plain teal bib apron held up by one single strap that rises from the two top corners of the bib and meets in a loop high behind her neck, so that seen from behind the whole of her back is plain white shirt with nothing on it except that one strap at the neck and the two waist ties passing round her waist to the front, the apron waist ties knotted in a bow at the front of her waist, dark navy trousers and plain black flat shoes
CafeCoworker.prompt_short: a young woman with dark brown hair in a short high ponytail, wearing a pure white short-sleeve shirt and a teal bib apron held up by one single strap that meets in a loop high behind her neck, her back otherwise plain white shirt with only the waist ties passing round it
CafeCoworker.prompt_apron: a plain teal bib apron with one single strap looped to go over the head and long waist ties
invariants: ONE neck loop, bare shirt back, ties knotted at the FRONT - the same apron pattern as CafeWalker, different colour.
Her shirt is PURE WHITE, never cream, never beige, never tan.
Short high ponytail, never loose hair, never a bun.
Her apron is teal. It is not the player's dark green.
CafeCoworker.never: cream shirt, beige shirt, tan shirt, crossed apron straps, cross-back apron, loose hair, bun, green apron, long sleeves
